While prior studies mainly focus on numeric characteris-tics, we extend their analysis by incorporating contextual narratives to derive contextualized account-level risk assessments.6 Additionally, obtaining access to private PCAOB inspection data will allow us to benchmark the quality of our predictions relative to human experts. Taken together, we expect that adding PCAOB’s private numerical information (e.g., audit hours, materiality Large Language Models and Financial Reporting Oversight 8 thresholds) and textual information (e.g., auditor notes submitted to the PCAOB, comment form) as model inputs will further improve our model’s predictive performance. Based on the above considerations, our first hypothesis in the alternate form is as follows: Hypothesis 1 Textual data processed with Large Language Models can improve the ability of the existing risk-assessment models, which rely on numerical data, to identify risks of restatements and can facilitate the detection of audit deficiencies. Relatedly, instead of processing the entire corpus of textual data with BERT, we will also leverage generative large language models to summarize information pertinent to audits and financial risks. results.title: The Rise of Out of Period Adjustments | Audit Analytics
results.content: For instance, if a company discovers a material misstatement in a previously-issued 10-K, the company would file a new 10-K for the prior period amended with the restated and corrected results. There are two options when correcting financial statements that are immaterially misstated: revision restatements or out of period adjustments. An out of period adjustment, on the other hand, is so immaterial — at least according to management — that it does not require any revision or restatement of prior period results. Instead, the company recognizes an adjustment in the current period to correct the error. A breakdown of the most referenced issues shows that the problems companies are correcting with out of period adjustments are fairly different from those corrected with restatements. (Note that some companies may identify multiple issues in a given adjustment/restatement). While classification issues are collectively referenced more than any other issue – 768 references – for restatements, very few companies make out of period adjustments to correct for classification issues. Only 74 out of period adjustments dealt with classification issues between 2010 and 2013.1. Though out of period adjustments are immaterial accounting errors, they can be a signal of weakness in a company’s reporting processes. One example is KBR, Inc. KBR’s financial reporting weaknesses can be seen in three stages: (1) Initial signals or red flags; (2) The out of period adjustment and related signals (more serious red flags); and (3) The seemingly inevitable Item 4.02 restatement (confirmation of red flags). When the 2013 annual statements were filed on February 27, 2014, KBR disclosed an out of period adjustment of $17 million in regards to revenue recognition. The previously reported $327 million net income was reduced to $171 million, which would have made the $17 million out of period adjustment a material error by almost any measure. On their own, out of period adjustments can indicate reporting problem areas, but when supplemented with other “red flags,” they may reveal pervasive deficiencies in a company’s financial reporting.

results.title: AQRM Red Flags: Financial Reporting - Audit Analytics
results.content: # AQRM Red Flags: Financial Reporting Posted on July 29, 2021 by Madeleine Conley *The Audit Analytics Accounting Quality + Risk Matrix (AQRM) makes it easy to identify accounting, audit, and governance red flags for public companies. This blog series breaks down the risks associated with specific firm-level events included in the AQRM.* Misstating financial statements is a significant accounting quality red flag. Unreliable financial statements reduce stakeholder confidence in companies and the ability of their control environment to prevent or detect errors. Misstatements also expose companies to increased shareholder litigation and regulatory risks. A report by professor Susan Scholz and the Center for Audit Quality (CAQ) found that “the average stock price reaction to restatements was -1.5%.” Returns were even more negative (-2.3%) for companies with Item 4.02 restatements. Big R restatements, or non-reliance restatements, are corrections of misstatements that are disclosed through the issuance of Item 4.02 on Form 8-K. Big R restatements are the most material restatements and are often accompanied by an ineffective internal control assessment. They also require the reissuance of previously issued financial statements to correct the misstatement. In addition to negative returns, reissuing financial statements can be costly. found that “the presence of restatements leads to higher audit fees in a subsequent period.” Further, a paper by Chakravarthy and Rajgopal found that, on average, companies take 2.2 actions to repair reputational damage post-restatement. This compares to just .31 actions, on average, in pre-restatement periods. Little r restatements, or revision restatements, are corrections of misstatements that are disclosed without reissuing previously issued financial statements. Though not as material, Scholz found that little r restatements result in -0.6% returns. However, companies that are required to make an adjustment to their financial statements also face challenges with their control environment and potential costs to strengthen their control environment. [KHC] has disclosed several restatements and adjustments over the past few years, including restatements related to revenue recognition. BorgWarner’s [BWA] 2018 Big R restatement resulted in both. The Audit Analytics Accounting Quality + Risk Matrix (AQRM) can be used to monitor, compare, and evaluate the severity of company misstatements along with many other “red flag” disclosures.

results.title: PCAOB Chair Williams Criticizes Restatements as Indicator of Audit Quality
results.content: # PCAOB Chair Williams Criticizes Restatements as Indicator of Audit Quality Soyoung Ho, Checkpoint News  Senior Editor Soyoung Ho, Checkpoint News  Senior Editor Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) Chair Erica Williams disputed arguments that the number of financial restatements is a good audit quality indicator, which has been relatively low in contrast to high audit deficiency rates identified during inspections in recent years. In particular, Ho accused the PCAOB of “painting a dire picture of the state of audit quality,” questioning whether the inspection and enforcement numbers that were emphasized to the public tell the entire story about the state of audit quality today. (See Board Member Ho Criticizes PCAOB for ‘Painting a Dire Picture’ of Audit Quality.) However, Williams, in her remarks, said that a proper audit should identify errors before restatements become necessary. “They’re just looking at something differently.” But Williams said Part I.A findings are serious because the audit firm did not obtain sufficient appropriate evidence to support its opinion, “and audit opinions were signed without completing the audit work required to verify the accuracy of the financial statements.” She explained that such deficiencies include a failure to perform procedures to test revenue or the costs of inventory. ### Related posts ### PCAOB Investor Panel Selects Best Critical, Key Audit Matters of 2024 The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board’s (PCAOB) Investor Advisory Group (IAG) presented three exemplary critical audit matters (CAMs) or key … ### Preliminary Inspection Results Show Improvement for Large Audit Firms This Year, PCAOB Acting Chair Says In a bit of good news, the quality of public company audits by the largest accounting firms continues to improve, … ### SEC Opens Comment Period on PCAOB’s Delay of Quality Control Standard Now that the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) on August 28, 2025, decided to postpone the implementation of its … ### More answers ### Trump, Commerce Secretary Discuss ‘Gold Card’ Program to Revamp EB-5 Visa Process in First Cabinet Meeting During a question and answer session at President Donald Trump’s first cabinet meeting on February 26, the 47th President engaged … ### After the Massive Tax Package, What’s Next for Congress?
